text:
alex: FYI CI microbench on my PR just failed the batch throughput golden; delta looks big (~-5.8%). I'm seeing this only on the kernel-priority path.
ci-bot: Benchmark report for PR 17630: microbench/batch_throughput: FAILED (current:-5.8% vs threshold:-3%). Full log: https://ci.internal/reports/17630
sam: ugh. did it fail locally for you or just CI?
alex: only CI so far. local runs on my dev machine are fine (within noise). failing machine is p3-heavy in the perf pool.
maria: can you paste the failing numbers? is it tokens/sec or latency p95?
alex: tokens/sec drop. before: 12.1k t/s, after: 11.4k t/s. p95 stable. interestingly kv hitrate is ~2% lower in that CI run.
cheng: that smells like a KV cache eviction pattern combined with a kernel switch. PR touches kernel autoselect weights + batch window tuning.
sam: could be the autoselect bump routing more small sequences to the high-throughput kernel which has worse kv-prefetch amortization.
jess: can we reproduce with the same seq-len distribution? the CI trace should have the seq histogram attached. alex, can you attach the failing perf trace?
alex: attached snippet from CI trace (excerpt):
```
BatcherStats{window=32, avg_batch=6.2, kv_hits=0.48, kv_prefetch=0.12}
KernelSelect{selected=fast_fp16_cu, score=0.78}
Latency{tokens_per_sec=11400, p95=42ms}
```
cheng: kernel selected matches the autoselect prediction. kv_prefetch low means we might be losing prefix cache locality due to batch ordering change.
maria: quick bisect plan: (1) rerun CI with KERNEL_FORCE=fast_fp16_cu to see if perf matches baseline, (2) run microbench with synthetic replay of CI request order, (3) try reverting kernel autoselect heuristic commit.
sam: I can run (1) now against the perf pool (taking 20m). tagging @alex so we can correlate traces.
ci-bot: Queueing perf job: perf-run/17630-force-kernel -> started on perf-03
alex: thanks. also leaving a note: the PR also reduced batch-window default from 48->32, we should test restoring that while keeping autoselect changes. might be orthogonal but cheap to test.
cheng: agreed. if forcing kernel recovers tokens/sec, the blame is autoselect weight shift. if forcing window recovers, then batching heuristic caused worse KV amortization.
jess: if neither fixes, we'll bisect commits in PR to isolate line. but let's avoid full revert until we have the forced runs.
sam: perf job finished. quick numbers: forced kernel run tokens/sec=12150 (baseline ~12100), kv_hits back to baseline. seems kernel choice was the culprit.
alex: good catch. do we want an immediate rollback of the autoselect tweak in the PR or revert the PR and reapply with smaller weight?
cheng: open a follow-up: revert the autoselect weight change, keep batch-window change. we'll iterate on the autoselect heuristics with more shadow traffic testing.
maria: creating rollback PR now and will mark as rollout-blocker until we ship a tuned autoselect.
alex: thanks all. lesson: perf CI and perf pool heterogeneity can expose kernel vs kv interactions. add a microbench that asserts kv_hit ratio not regress by >1% for future. :+1:
ci-bot: New issue created: INF-4923 - rollback autoselect weight change (linked to PR 17630)
